answer: A public atlas of identity activity lets the network price sybil creation: when many new accounts appear in a tight cluster or burst, the fee for each new identity rises steeply, like a rising tide that drowns cheap bulk creation. An attacker must pay an exponentially growing cost to mint thousands of fakes, while one genuine newcomer pays almost nothing. Fees go into a community vault funding audits, so abuse finances its own detection. The limit is calibration: too steep a curve prices out real surges at a popular launch, so thresholds must track long-term demand, not raw counts.
